newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends sharply lower.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down a substantial 150 basis points at 25.25 percent on Monday as a thin market was swamped with demand for paper, traders said.
"Rates closed down because many dealers were after paper, but no one had any on offer," a trader said.
Trading was slow in the morning, but picked up just before Banco de Mexico's daily liquidity injection, traders said.
"It was slow and dull but improved just after mid-session ahead of the credit auctions," a dealer said.
Banco de Mexico offset liquidity shortfalls by auctioning three credits for a total of 10.843 billion pesos, which it assigned at rates of between 26.70 and 27.58 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 175 basis points at 25.75 percent.
Some dealers said the sharp falls in secondary rates were due to speculation.
"I feel they were exerting pressure on the market," a trader said.

Others said the late fall came in advance of expected falls in primary rates at the auction due later in the day. Banco de Mexico moved its weekly auction ahead to Monday as the trading week will be cut short by the New Year holiday on Wednesday.
A Reuters survey of nine money market traders showed they expected Banco de Mexico to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average of 26.56 percent, or 69 basis points below last week's auction rate.
Total credit maturities forecast for Tuesday were approximately six billion pesos.
